candidates.title: Demagnetize a solid robot-joint shaft through a low-frequency tunnel
candidates.objective: Grasp a representative solid ferromagnetic robot-joint shaft, align it with a round low-frequency demagnetizing tunnel, physically carry its full length through the alternating-field region, and place it in a clean output cradle with reduced simulated remanence, without collision, dropping, reversal-induced remagnetization, or particle recontamination.
skills: stable grasping of an elongated rigid shaft
orientation control under pose-dependent magnetic forces
candidates.success_conditions: Full success requires every shaft material cell to traverse the effective field, a validated hysteresis calculation to finish below the frozen representative remanence threshold, stable placement in the clean cradle, and no tunnel contact, drop, unsafe release, contamination-zone contact, or excessive device thermal load. Alignment and incomplete treatment earn partial credit. Waypoint traversal alone, direct magnetic-state writes, pose or velocity injection, collision suppression, or a hidden success flag cannot score. A physically valid one-arm strategy receives full credit.
candidates.industrial_value: The manufacturer identifies shafts as suitable products for low-frequency tunnel demagnetization. Separate bearing-industry guidance requires demagnetizing components that contact bearings and documents particle adhesion, denting, vibration, and wear from residual magnetism. A representative robot-joint shaft treated before bearing assembly therefore has direct robot-building relevance.
candidates.dexterity: The central manipulation is carrying a long, solid part through a confined aperture while preserving clearance and orientation as its magnetic state and field-derived forces evolve. It is materially harder than pick-and-place, yet remains a rigid-body task within pinned-YAM reach after fixture scaling; no artificial bimanual requirement is imposed.

evidence.locator: Industrial magnetic handling and demagnetization brochure, page 18, “Low-frequency demagnetizing tunnels”
Industrial magnetic handling and demagnetization brochure, page 18, “Low-frequency demagnetizing tunnels”
Modelica Magnetic FluxTubes UsersGuide, StaticHysteresis.Tellinen, “The Tellinen hysteresis model”

candidates.asset_plan: Author a representative, explicitly non-product-replica rigid tunnel, 320 mm solid shaft, input stand, clean output cradle, and guarded field enclosure. Freeze aperture, shaft diameter and mass, field-zone length, material envelope curve, remanence limit, force ceiling, thermal duty, and reach bounds before development. Use a Tellinen hysteresis state per axial shaft cell, driven only by simulated coil field evaluated from actual poses and time in the verified native PRE/POST physics callback. Couple a bounded field-gradient force and torque into PhysX; never overwrite shaft pose, velocity, or magnetic state. Before YAM integration, test major and minor loops, proper and incomplete passage, reversal, stopping, timestep/rate convergence, force and energy finiteness, thermal accumulation, reset freshness, collision response, and reachable clean placement. The representative field calibration and protocol are disclosed prototype assumptions, not manufacturer specifications.
candidates.risk: No acquired source supplies a specific tunnel model’s proprietary aperture, waveform, field calibration, or operating speed. Those values must remain frozen representative assumptions and cannot be advertised as Goudsmit performance. Static Tellinen behavior does not by itself establish dynamic eddy-current accuracy, so the selected solid shaft must use a conservative low-frequency regime and pass convergence and improper-treatment controls. Catalog neighbor pr-1810 tests controlled passage through a narrow slot; final novelty depends on the independently validated remanence outcome and magnetic force interaction, not on the passage trajectory alone. Full catalog and six-suite clearance remains a mandatory downstream gate.

candidates.title: Demagnetize a thin robot-reducer gear blank over a plate device
candidates.objective: Pick a representative sub-10-mm ferromagnetic robot-reducer gear blank, expose its complete area to a plate demagnetizer through a controlled parallel sweep and retreat, then place it in a clean inspection tray with physically reduced remanence and no plate strike, drop, untreated region, or thermal overload.
skills: controlled retreat from an alternating field
candidates.success_conditions: Full success requires every discretized gear region to receive sufficient pose-derived alternating-field exposure, final remanence below a frozen threshold, stable clean placement, and no plate contact, drop, missed sector, reversal-induced remagnetization, or duty-limit violation. Mere tabletop placement or coverage waypoints do not score.
candidates.industrial_value: The manufacturer describes plate demagnetizers for flat magnetic products and machine construction, while its industrial report identifies bearing wear, adhering chips, and magnetic-sensor errors as consequences of unwanted magnetism. A thin precision gear is geometrically compatible, but the acquired evidence does not specifically identify robot-reducer gears.
candidates.dexterity: The robot must hold a broad, thin part nearly parallel to the plate while controlling stand-off, coverage, and retreat. This tests surface-following and orientation control rather than generic transport.

candidates.asset_plan: Use a rigid procedural plate device and thin gear blank. If pursued, distribute hysteresis cells over the gear, derive exposure from actual pose and field decay, and validate missed-sector, excessive-height, reversal, contact, thermal, reset, and timestep controls before robot integration.
candidates.risk: The acquired manufacturer material establishes product class and thickness but not a manual treatment path, working stand-off, retreat distance, field profile, device geometry, or duty cycle. Direct robot-reducer manufacturing relevance is also inferential rather than explicitly sourced. A coverage counter would be an invalid substitute for the missing physical mechanism.
missing_evidence: A model-consistent plate-demagnetizer operating procedure and verified diagram
Direct primary-source evidence that the selected robot-reducer component requires this treatment
Validated field-versus-height and spatial hysteresis behavior for full-area treatment
Complete catalog comparison against surface-processing and magnetic-fixturing tasks

candidates.title: Demagnetize a bearing-assembly mandrel with a portable bar
candidates.objective: Manipulate a portable demagnetizing bar around the accessible cylindrical and shoulder surfaces of a fixtured bearing-assembly mandrel, maintaining the required pose and coverage so all remanent hot spots are physically reduced without tool contact, missed regions, overheating, or unsafe release.
candidates.success_conditions: Full success requires all initially magnetized mandrel regions to finish below a frozen remanence limit, the bar to remain collision-free and within its thermal duty, and both objects to end stably placed. Missed hot spots, excessive stand-off, contact, drop, or direct state mutation fail or receive partial credit.
candidates.industrial_value: The bearing-industry application note explicitly requires checking and demagnetizing bearing-contact tools. The equipment manufacturer identifies demagnetizing bars for tools and machine parts in difficult-to-reach locations, including machine building and toolmaking shops.
candidates.dexterity: This tests controlled tool orientation and curved-surface coverage in constrained access. It can require a real regrasp to reach the mandrel shoulder, but one-arm completion must score if the sourced physical treatment is achieved.

evidence.locator: Industrial magnetic handling and demagnetization brochure, page 18, “Demagnetization bars”
Industrial magnetic handling and demagnetization brochure, page 18, “Demagnetization bars”

candidates.asset_plan: Author a rigid representative bearing-contact mandrel and portable bar only after obtaining the matching device instructions. Use spatial hysteresis cells and pose-derived fields, then validate coverage sensitivity, retreat behavior, magnetic forces, thermal duty, contact failures, and reset determinism.
candidates.risk: The brochure does not provide bar dimensions, stand-off, orientation, sweep speed, overlap, retreat method, field calibration, or duty limit. The bearing note’s instruction to scan an entire surface concerns measurement and cannot be reused as a treatment procedure. Without a bar manual, the essential treatment action would be invented.
missing_evidence: Portable-bar manufacturer operating instructions and independently verified diagram
Sourced stand-off, orientation, sweep, retreat, and duty constraints
Validated spatial field and hysteresis model
Complete catalog comparison against inspection and surface-coverage objectives

selection_reason: The shaft-tunnel objective is the only candidate whose acquired manufacturer evidence directly matches both the component form—solid shafts—and the required device class—low-frequency tunnels—while bearing-industry evidence supplies direct robot-joint manufacturing significance. Its essential material-state mechanism has an established hysteresis formulation and can be driven from real simulated pose and time rather than a waypoint flag. Unknown proprietary calibration and exact product dimensions are bounded, disclosed prototype assumptions suitable for component testing, not unknown retention or contact mechanisms. The plate and portable-bar alternatives lack sourced treatment procedures and component-specific grounding, so they remain research-needed. Selection is readiness to attempt native component validation; it does not assert completed physics tests, YAM demos, or final catalog and six-suite novelty clearance.
